Standard: The air vehicle has acceptable flight performance and satisfactory workload during AR operations throughout the AR envelope. a. Boom Tanker. Tanker flight performance during refueling operations is assessed as no worse than a rating of 6 from MIL-STD-1797, Cooper-Harper rating scale figure (or equivalent rating system) and receiver motion does not adversely impact tanker ability to maintain commanded attitude, altitude, or airspeed. AR maneuvers include straight and level flight, turns, toboggans, climbs, and breakaway maneuvers throughout the AR envelope. b. Drogue Tanker. Tanker flight performance during refueling operations is assessed as no worse than a rating of 6 from MIL-STD-1797, Cooper-Harper rating scale figure (or equivalent rating system) and receiver motion does not adversely impact ability to maintain commanded attitude, altitude, or airspeed. AR maneuvers include straight and level flight, turns, toboggans, climbs, and breakaway maneuvers throughout the AR envelope. c. Receptacle Receiver. Receiver flight performance during refueling operations is assessed as no worse than a rating of 6 from MIL-STD-1797, Cooper-Harper rating scale figure (or equivalent rating system), including closing and stabilizing in contact position, station keeping throughout the boom envelope, straight and level flight, turns, toboggans, climbs, and breakaway maneuvers throughout the AR envelope. d. Probe Receiver. Receiver flight performance during refueling operations is assessed as no worse than a rating of 6 from MIL-STD-1797, Cooper-Harper rating scale figure (or equivalent rating system), including contacts at closure rates up to 10 ft/s, stabilizing post contact, maneuvering in and out of refuel zone, station keeping, straight and level flight, turns, climbs, and breakaway maneuvers throughout the AR envelope. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analysis of aerodynamic environment and air vehicle performance shows that the air vehicle has power and control authority to execute AR maneuvers with targeted air vehicles. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Ground based piloted simulation verifies the air vehicle has power and control authority to execute AR maneuvers with targeted air vehicles. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Flight evaluations of air vehicle performance, including predictability of response, stability and control, control sensitivity, time delay, oscillations, PIO tendencies, undesirable motions, workload and HQRs verify tanker flight performance is assessed as no worse than a rating of 6 from MIL-STD-1797, Cooper-Harper rating scale figure (or equivalent system) during AR operations. Test points include station keeping with targeted receiver air vehicles in contact and pre-contact positions in straight and level flight, turning, and toboggans, throughout the AR envelope, at worst-case combinations of tanker and receiver gross weights and CGs. b. Drogue Tanker. Flight evaluations of air vehicle performance, including predictability of response, stability and control, control sensitivity, time delay, oscillations, PIO tendencies, undesirable motions, workload and HQRs verify tanker flight performance is assessed as no worse than a rating of 6 from MIL-STD-1797, Cooper-Harper rating scale figure (or equivalent system) during AR operations. Test points include straight and level flight, turning, and toboggans with targeted receiver air vehicles in contact and refueling positions, throughout the AR envelope, at worst-case combinations of tanker and receiver gross weights and CGs. c. Receptacle Receiver. Flight evaluations of air vehicle performance, including predictability of response, stability and control, control sensitivity, time delay, oscillations, PIO tendencies, undesirable motions, workload and HQRs verify receiver flight performance is assessed as no worse than a rating of 6 from MIL-STD-1797, Cooper-Harper rating scale figure (or equivalent system) during AR operations. Test points include station keeping, with targeted tanker air vehicles, pre-contact and in contact positions throughout the boom envelope, in straight and level flight, turning, and toboggans, at worst-case combinations of tanker and receiver gross weights and CGs, throughout the AR envelope. d. Probe Receiver. Flight evaluations of air vehicle performance, including predictability of response, stability and control, control sensitivity, time delay, oscillations, PIO tendencies, undesirable motions, workload and HQRs verify receiver flight performance is assessed as no worse than a rating of 6 from MIL-STD-1797, Cooper-Harper rating scale figure (or equivalent system) during AR operations. Test points include wake surveys at pre-contact, contact and at the inner refueling limit, contacts at closure rates up to 10 ft/s, stabilizing post contact, maneuvering in and out of refuel zone, station keeping in straight and level flight and turns, and breakaway throughout the AR envelope, at worst-case combinations of tanker and receiver gross weights and CGs.
